findings.title: Full traceability of success criteria and migration plan to tasks
findings.description:
Description: I mapped each success criterion and each Migration Plan row to a task and found full coverage with no orphaned or missing items.
- "No build path reads/writes `adoption.state`, runs detection, or spawns `sq`" → seam removal (3.3), `writeAdoptionState` deletion (4.3), probe deletion (4.4), grep gates (3.3, 4.x, 6.2), and the fake-`sq` marker assertion in 5.1.
- "Phase 0 brownfield build returns the concept prompt and writes nothing, whatever `adoption.state` holds" → 5.1 (runs the no-toml and `in_progress` states, asserts tree/bytes unchanged + concept prompt + no `### Adoption Facts` + no `sq` marker) and 6.3 walkthrough.
- "Greenfield, already-planned, later-phase builds byte-identical" → 2.1/2.2 (captured pre-cut) + 3.7/6.1 re-guards.
- "CLI and MCP `context_build` outputs match" → 5.1 parity check + 6.3.
- "`MIN_GUIDE_VERSION` warning still on stderr (CLI) / separate from context (MCP)" → preserved in 3.5/3.6, re-asserted in 6.1 with the exact, verified test titles.
- "services/ imports nothing from adoption/ or detection/" → 3.3 grep + 6.2 grep (both verified achievable: the only `services/` importers are `ContextIntegrator.ts:10` and `CoreServiceFactory.ts:12-14`, all removed in 3.3).
- "No exported symbol remains that only deleted code used (except history/comprehensionAnalysis/adoptionOutcome)" → 6.2 export audit keyed to the design's Interfaces Required.
- "Format, lint, typecheck, full test pass" → 6.1.
Every Migration Plan row (resolver/facts/completion, `contracts.ts`, `adoptionState.ts`, `adoptionOutcome.ts`, both `index.ts`, probe + exports, `CoreServiceFactory`, `ContextIntegrator`, `ContextTemplateEngine`, `SectionBuilder`/`context.ts`, `node.ts`, `build.ts`, `contextTools.ts`, `integrationSetup.ts`) and every delete/edit test file is covered. No task traces to work outside the design.

findings.title: Sequencing is acyclic and the pre-cut golden capture is enforced
findings.description: Description: Section 2 (golden capture, D6) explicitly runs "before any source edit" and commits at 2.3, so the byte-identity test is anchored to the old code as D6 requires; it is then re-run after the cut (3.7, 6.1) with the invariant "a golden file that must change is a defect." The seam removal is split so each commit compiles: 3.1–3.2 stop rendering fields that still exist and commit at 3.2a; 3.3–3.6 change the `createContextPipeline` signature and both callers and commit together at 3.7. The file correctly notes the cross-package compile constraint (`cli`/`mcp-server` typecheck against core's built `dist/`) and instructs `pnpm --filter @context-forge/core build` at 3.4 before 3.5, and that between 3.4 and 3.6 only `mcp-server` typecheck fails. Deletions in section 4 each leave the workspace compiling and commit individually. No circular dependencies.

findings.title: Deletion-commit grep gates silently depend on earlier deletions
findings.description: Description: The per-task `grep` success criteria in section 4 (e.g. 4.3's `grep -rn "writeAdoptionState|adoption-completed"` over `packages/*/src packages/*/tests`) only return empty because section 4.1 has already deleted the test files that still referenced those names (e.g. `adoptionCompletion.test.ts:22` and `adoptionBuild.integration.test.ts:185-214` call `writeAdoptionState`; `adoptionFacts.test.ts:60` references `adoption-completed`). I traced every current reference to the grepped symbols and confirmed all are either in files deleted by 4.1/4.4 or explicitly removed by the named task, so each gate is satisfiable in the prescribed order. This is correct behavior for an ordered deletion, not a defect — recorded only so the ordering is not accidentally "fixed" by re-running a later grep standalone (it would appear to fail out of order).

findings.title: Purity test reuses a fixture helper that is deleted mid-file via `git show`
findings.description: Description: Task 5.1 recreates `createBrownfieldCheckout` by reading it back with `git show {target}:.../adoptionParity.test.ts`, since 3.6 deletes that file. I confirmed `createBrownfieldCheckout` exists at `packages/mcp-server/tests/integration/adoptionParity.test.ts:67` and that the steps it performs (copy `fixtures/integration-project`, install the `brownfield-guide` prompt, write ≥2000 source lines, add a comprehension document, no planning artifacts) match both the design's D5 fixture and the task's step list. This is a reasonable, non-circular way to port the setup to the new in-process purity test and is consistent with the design's "Special Considerations" (fake `sq` on `PATH` for the test process only; MCP runs in-process). No action needed.
